findings.title: Crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: In EventManager.create, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` is followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. organizer has no calendar app installed) and the event location is Google Meet — exactly the 'Meet selected w/o a Google Cal' scenario this code is meant to handle — `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and reading `.integration` throws a TypeError, aborting the whole booking creation. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` which was null-safe. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` (or better, `some(cal => cal.integration === "google_calendar")` now that it is an array).

findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for organization slug
findings.body: The change `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` inverts the logic. Previously the slug was set immediately only when team billing was disabled (with billing enabled, the org pays first and the slug is assigned later from `requestedSlug` in metadata). Now the slug is set at creation time when billing IS enabled — bypassing the payment-gated slug assignment flow — and is never set when billing is disabled, leaving organizations without a slug/subdomain. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and looks accidental; it should be reverted to the negated condition.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent fallback find() is dead code and loses destination calendar
findings.body: In updateEvent, `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` — in the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so `find()` can never match anything and `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`. `calendar.events.update` is then called with `calendarId: undefined`, which fails. The same pattern in deleteEvent (line 315) falls through to `"primary"`, so the event is deleted from the wrong calendar (or 404s silently) instead of the destination calendar. The fallback should use the first destination calendar's externalId (the pre-PR behavior), e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses selectedCalendar without the 'primary' fallback
findings.body: In createEvent, the insert call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` that adds the hangout link to the description uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` with no fallback. When no destination calendar matches the current `credentialId` (so `selectedCalendar` is undefined), the event is created on `primary` but the patch is sent with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so meeting links never make it into the event description. The patch should use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value as the insert.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services still only use the first destination calendar
findings.body: Office365 (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), Lark (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128) and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) all read only the first element of the now-array `destinationCalendar`. Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination with each host's own credential, for a collective event with multiple hosts on these providers the second host's credential is used against the first host's `externalId`, creating the event in the wrong calendar or failing with an auth/404 error. Only the Google service was adapted (find by credentialId), so the multi-host fix this PR claims only works for Google Calendar. The same per-credential selection is needed in these services.

findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: For COLLECTIVE events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. But `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar (the ternary chain ends in `null`). Optional chaining makes the push a no-op in that case, so team members' destination calendars are silently discarded — precisely the collective scenario the PR is meant to fix — and no calendar events get created for those hosts. The code should assign `evt.destinationCalendar = teamDestinationCalendars` when it is null rather than relying on `?.push`.

findings.title: organization select removed from dynamic-booking user query
findings.body: The refactored `loadUsers` for the no-eventTypeId (dynamic link) branch drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the prisma.user.findMany select that the previous code included. Any downstream logic for dynamic bookings that reads `user.organization` (e.g. organization-aware routing/slug building for dynamic group bookings) will now see `undefined` and behave as if the user belongs to no organization. This removal is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change and looks accidental; the select should be restored.

findings.title: Breaking change to webhook payload destinationCalendar shape
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is sent verbatim in BOOKING_* webhook payloads, and its shape changes from a single `DestinationCalendar` object (or null) to an array. External webhook subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId` etc. will break with no migration note, even though the PR is marked 'non-breaking'. Additionally the empty value is inconsistent across emitters: handleNewBooking emits `null` while confirm/cancel/payment handlers emit `[]` (see the e2e expectations at lines 119 `null` vs 249 `[]`), so consumers must handle both. This should be documented as a breaking webhook change and the empty representation unified.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes each booking event once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch now lives inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop over all calendar references, and for each reference it iterates ALL of the organizer's calendar credentials × ALL updated bookings, calling deleteEvent. With multiple calendar references (the multi-host case this PR introduces) the same booking's calendar event is deleted N times, and it is deleted with whichever credentials the organizer happens to have rather than the reference's own credential. At best this produces duplicate delete calls (only tolerated because Google treats 410/404 as success); other providers may error and surface as a failed cancellation.

findings.title: No tests for the new multi-destination collective behavior
findings.body: The PR checklist explicitly states no tests were added. The core change — destinationCalendar becoming an array, per-credential calendar selection in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, Google's find-by-credentialId, and the collective push of team calendars — is only covered by an updated e2e assertion for BOOKING_REJECTED. Unit tests for EventManager (create/reschedule/cancel with multiple destination calendars, empty destinationCalendar + Google Meet location, destination calendars without credentialId) are missing, which is how the crash at EventManager.ts:119 and the `?.push` no-op escaped review.
